name: Pass Thurn
kurzbeschreibung: Pass Thurn (1,274 m) links Kitzbühel with Salzburg's Pinzgau: protected Wasenmoos bog, sweeping mountain views, and hiking paradise.
preis: Pass summit and federal road B161 toll-free; Wasenmoos nature trail freely accessible
beschreibung:
Overview

The storied and scenic Pass Thurn lies at an elevation of 1,274 meters, forming an idyllic alpine passage between the Kitzbühel Alps in Tyrol and the upper Salzach Valley in Salzburg province. Nestled between the gentle grassy slopes of the Resterkogel and the rugged peaks of the Kitzbühel range, the pass road connects the famous Tyrolean town of Kitzbühel via Jochberg with Mittersill. Merchants and travelers have traversed this saddle since the Bronze Age more than three thousand years ago to transport copper ores extracted from local mines. Today, the pass summit serves as a versatile recreation area, celebrated in summer for lush pastures and the protected Wasenmoos peat bog, while in winter the KitzSki Resterhöhe gondola whisks skiers straight into world-class ski terrain.

Route & Requirements

The mountain pass offers a tranquil, barrier-free natural retreat for leisurely walkers, botanists, and families. Directly at the summit begins the Wasenmoos nature discovery trail: A well-maintained wooden boardwalk leads barrier-free and pushchair-accessible through an internationally protected raised bog of European significance (walking time approx. 1 hour, very easy). Informative displays explain carnivorous sundew plants, cranberries, and rare dragonflies. For enthusiastic hikers, Pass Thurn is the ideal starting point for panoramic tours to the Resterkogel (1,894 m) or onwards to the Zweitausender (2,004 m), offering stunning vistas toward the glaciated peaks of the Hohe Tauern. Sturdy ankle-high hiking boots and windproof layers are advised for mountain ascents, whereas standard walking shoes suffice for the Wasenmoos boardwalk.

Visit & Arrival

The pass road along the B161 federal highway remains open 24 hours daily throughout the year and is completely toll-free. Generous free parking is available directly at the pass summit and at the base station of the Resterhöhe cable car. By public transit, take trains to Kitzbühel or Mittersill; regional bus line 4010 connects both stations at frequent intervals, stopping right at the summit and main trailheads.

Tips

Stroll across the wooden walkways of Wasenmoos around sunset, when the snow-capped three-thousand-meter peaks of the Hohe Tauern mirror beautifully in still peat pools. Drop into the cozy alpine inn at the pass summit to savor authentic Tyrolean Kaspressknödel with fresh cabbage salad.
